history.reason: Issue 4 poses a clear, falsifiable research question (does joint modeling improve prediction?) with identified tractability concerns (data availability) and concrete next steps, whereas Issue 3 proposes applying TextGrad methodologically without establishing why TextGrad specifically solves the stated problem or how success would be measured objectively.

Issue 3 has clearer tractability and falsifiability for six months: a concrete hypothesis (TextGrad outperforms static aggregation) with a defined evaluation pathway. Issue 4, while higher-impact and more novel in scope, defers its core feasibility question (data availability) to future work and risks becoming bottlenecked on dataset discovery rather than research contribution.
